title: The raw alteration generators admit pullbacks and are stable under them
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\ell$ be a prime. In $\mathcal C=\operatorname{alt}/S$ [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], let $K(X)$ consist precisely of the presieves represented by either (i) a set-indexed $\ell'$-decomposed etale family $(U_i\to X)_i$, or (ii) a singleton proper surjective maximally $\ell'$-finite morphism $U\to X$, with these terms as defined in that definition node. A presieve is a set of arrows with a fixed target. For every arrow $Y\to X$ of $\mathcal C$ and every family of type (i) or (ii), the categorical pullbacks $U_i\times_X^{\mathcal C}Y$ exist, and their projections to $Y$ form a family of the same type. These are categorical pullbacks in $\mathcal C$, characterized by the universal property of a commuting square [def-pc-fibre-product], and are not asserted to be the ordinary scheme fibre products. Consequently $K$ (a precoverage, i.e. a collection of designated presieves) has pullbacks, and is stable under base change in the sense that for every $R\in K(X)$ and every arrow $Y\to X$, the presieve formed by the projections to $Y$ of one chosen categorical pullback of each arrow of $R$ belongs to $K(Y)$. No stability under composition of these raw families is asserted.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.2.6 (existence of categorical pullbacks), Proposition 1.2.7 (maximal prime-to-ell finiteness under base change), Proposition 1.2.8 (proper surjectivity under dominant reduction), 2.1.1 and Remark 2.3.2, printed pp.25--28.

proof.text: For any two arrows $U\to X\leftarrow Y$, apply only the fibre-product assertion of [lem-per-alteration-cover-calculus]: the categorical pullback exists and is $Q=(U\times_XY)_{\mathrm{md}}$ relative to $S$. This assertion concerns existence and the object, not merely the preservation of covering sieves; we do not use that node to infer preservation of raw generators. Each of $X,Y,U,Q$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$. By [lem-per-alteration-arrow-properties], their arrows are finite type and send component generic points to component generic points with finite residue extensions. In particular every generic point $y$ of $Y$ maps to a generic point $x$ of $X$ and a generic point $s$ of $S$. All four schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

source.place: Expose II 1.1.10 and Proposition 1.2.6, printed pp.24--25.

proof.text: First take an etale generating family $(U_i\to X)_i$. Write $P_i=U_i\times_XY$. Its projection $P_i\to Y$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Apply the etale comparison in [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection] over $S$ to $P_i\to Y$: both schemes are finite type over $S$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and Step 1. Since every generic point of $Y$ lies over a generic point of $S$, the closed set defining $Y_{\mathrm{md}}$ in that cited statement is all of $Y$; as $Y$ is reduced, the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] applied to $\mathrm{id}_Y$ gives $Y_{\mathrm{md}}=Y$. It gives $Q_i=(P_i)_{\mathrm{md}}\simeq P_i\times_Y Y_{\mathrm{md}}=P_i$ compatibly with the projections. Hence the categorical pullback projections are etale.

For any point $y\in Y$ over $x\in X$, choose $i$ and $u\in U_i$ over $x$ with finite residue degree prime to $\ell$, using the definition of decomposedness [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Apply [lem-per-prime-to-ell-residue-base-change] with $k=\kappa(x)$, $L=\kappa(u)$ and $K=\kappa(y)$. The point description [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] places its good point in $P_i$ above $(u,y)$; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] identifies its residue extension over $\kappa(y)$ with the one supplied by the residue-degree lemma. Thus $P_i\to Y$, and by Step 2 also $Q_i\to Y$, have a good lift of every $y$. This proves precisely the etale generating condition, for any set of indices, without extracting a finite subfamily.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.2.7 and 2.1.1, printed pp.25--26.

proof.text: Now take a proper surjective maximally $\ell\prime$-finite $U\to X$. Its ordinary pullback $P=U\times_XY\to Y$ is proper and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. These are finite-type $S$-schemes by Step 1 and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The proper-surjective assertion of [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection] therefore gives a proper surjective $Q=P_{\mathrm{md}}\to Y_{\mathrm{md}}=Y$. It remains to check the generic residue-degree condition; properness and surjectivity alone do not imply it.

Let $y$ be a component generic point of $Y$, with images $x$ in $X$ and $s$ in $S$. Step 1 makes $x,s$ generic. Surjectivity of $U\to X$ and maximal $\ell\prime$-finiteness [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology] provide a generic $u$ above $x$ of degree prime to $\ell$. The same residue-degree and fibre-product-point lemmas as in Step 3 give $p\in P$ over $(u,y)$ of finite degree prime to $\ell$ over $\kappa(y)$. This point lies over $s$, hence belongs to the support of $P_{\mathrm{md}}$ by [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection]. Its lift $q\in Q$ has the same residue field: locally the reduced induced closed immersion is $A\to A/I$ and residue fields at primes containing $I$ are unchanged [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Choose a component generic generalization $q_0$ of $q$ using [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover, lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Its image in $Y$ generalizes the generic point $y$, hence equals $y$. The arrow assertion of Step 1 gives finite $\kappa(q_0)/\kappa(y)$. By [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre], $q_0$ is closed in the fibre $Q_y$. The fibre $Q_y$ is homeomorphic to the subspace of points of $Q$ over $y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and $q$ lies in the closure of $q_0$ inside that subspace, so $q=q_0$. Thus the good lift is generic, as required. All generic residue extensions of $Q\to Y$ are already finite by Step 1. This proves maximal $\ell\prime$-finiteness.

source.place: Expose II Propositions 1.2.6--1.2.8, printed pp.25--26; generic-point verification expanded from 1.1.10.

proof.text: For $R\in K(X)$, choose a representing family of either type. Step 1 supplies its pullbacks, and Steps 2--5 show that their projections again represent a member of $K(Y)$. Repeated arrows in the representation make no difference to the presieve. Any other chosen categorical pullback is uniquely isomorphic to this one over both factors by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]; an isomorphism preserves properness, etaleness, surjectivity, generic points and the induced residue extensions, so the same family condition holds for that choice. This is exactly having pullbacks and stability under base change as defined in the item. For the empty target the empty etale family and the proper singleton with empty source satisfy the same argument vacuously. No composition of raw families has been used.
